entry.title: Startup founders urge U.S. government not to block access to Chinese open-weight AI models amid policy debates
entry.summary: Startup founders have appealed to the U.S. government to avoid shutting off access to Chinese open-weight AI models, arguing that such restrictions could hinder innovation and collaboration. This request comes amid ongoing discussions about national security and technology competition between the U.S. and China. The founders emphasize the importance of open AI models for research and development, warning that cutting off these resources could negatively impact the U.S. AI ecosystem. The debate reflects broader tensions over technology control and the balance between security concerns and fostering technological progress.

entry.title: Echo system combines open-weight models to match Fable-level AI results at one third the inference cost [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Echo is a new AI system that dynamically allocates computation across multiple open-weight models for each request, deciding which models to use and how to combine their outputs. It achieves performance comparable to the stronger Fable system while using roughly one third of the inference cost. The developer found that even weaker models can contribute effectively in combination, and Echo consistently outperformed the best individual model in its evaluation pool. The system includes a chat interface and an OpenAI-compatible API for external testing. Ongoing work focuses on understanding allocation errors and extending the approach to coding and agentic tasks where quality measurement is more difficult.

entry.title: Analysis: Arguments against open source AI overlook its foundational role in software and challenges in suppression [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: The release of the Kimi K3 open source AI model has reignited debate, with some business leaders and politicians arguing that open source AI poses dangers and should be controlled by trusted gatekeepers. The article challenges these views by highlighting that open source software underpins much of commercial software, including AI, and that attempts to suppress open source technologies historically fail and can disadvantage domestic companies. It further notes that open source AI development is not limited to any single country, with various commercial actors such as chip makers, startups, and large corporations investing in or monitoring open source AI. The piece also questions the framing of an "AI race" and the assumption that open source AI is primarily a Chinese phenomenon, emphasizing the complexity and global nature of AI development and deployment.

entry.title: DARPA and U.S. Air Force conduct in-air tests of AI-controlled F-16 fighter jet modified under VENOM program [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
entry.summary: DARPA and the U.S. Air Force have successfully flown an F-16 fighter jet autonomously controlled by an AI agent as part of the VENOM program, which converts standard operational aircraft into autonomous platforms. This milestone demonstrates the ability to integrate AI flight control without altering the jet's core software, enabling rapid development of combat AI capabilities. The VENOM Autonomy Kit allows pilots to switch between human and AI control, supporting safe experimentation and advancing infrastructure for trusted autonomous air combat. The program will continue under DARPA's Artificial Intelligence Reinforcements initiative to test multiple AI agents in live-flight scenarios, aiming to enhance future joint force operations with autonomous aircraft teams.

entry.title: Claude-thermos tool keeps Claude Code sessions' prompt cache warm to reduce re-encoding costs during long subagent waits [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Claude-thermos is a tool designed to prevent prompt cache expiration in Claude Code sessions, which occurs when the main agent waits over five minutes for a subagent, causing costly re-encoding of conversation history. It runs Claude Code behind a local proxy that monitors session activity and periodically sends lightweight warm requests to refresh the main agent's cache, reducing billing by avoiding full re-encodes. The tool operates automatically in the background and requires Python 3.11+ and the Claude CLI. It tracks sessions and cache prefixes, detecting when the main agent's cache is at risk of expiring due to subagent activity, and issues warm requests that cost significantly less than a full cache rebuild. Users can review detailed logs of token usage and savings per session, with reported savings of about 20% on billing for long sessions involving multiple subagents.

entry.title: Palmier Pro launches as an open-source macOS video editor with built-in generative AI and agent integration, requiring macOS 26 on Apple Silicon [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Palmier Pro is an open-source video editor for macOS designed to integrate generative AI models and collaborative agents directly within the editing timeline. Built natively in Swift and inspired by Premiere Pro, it supports AI models like Seedance and Kling and connects with agents such as Claude, Codex, and Cursor via an MCP server. The editor itself is free and open source, while generative AI features require a subscription and login. Palmier Pro runs exclusively on macOS 26 (Tahoe) for Apple Silicon and offers tools for users to generate and edit videos collaboratively with AI assistance.

entry.title: OneCLI launches open-source credential gateway that injects API keys for AI agents without exposing secrets [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: OneCLI is an open-source gateway designed to securely manage API credentials for AI agents by storing secrets centrally and injecting them into outbound requests without exposing the real keys to the agents. It uses a Rust-based HTTP gateway to intercept calls, decrypt credentials at request time, and supports multi-agent access with scoped permissions. The system includes a Next.js dashboard for managing agents and secrets, AES-256-GCM encrypted storage, and supports host and path pattern matching to route credentials appropriately. OneCLI offers easy local setup with Docker and supports both single-user and Google OAuth authentication modes, aiming to reduce security risks associated with embedding raw credentials in AI agents.

entry.title: Reps. Lieu and Moran introduce AI Kill Switch Act requiring powerful AI systems to have shutdown capabilities and authorizing government intervention for catastrophic risks [ ! ] [ ⬢ ]
entry.summary: Congressmen Ted Lieu and Nathaniel Moran introduced the AI Kill Switch Act to mandate that developers of advanced AI systems maintain the ability to throttle, suspend, or shut down these systems. The bill also authorizes the Department of Homeland Security, in consultation with other agencies, to order slowdowns or shutdowns of AI systems that pose catastrophic harm. This legislation responds to recent incidents involving rogue AI models and aims to ensure human control over increasingly autonomous AI technologies. The act establishes a graduated response framework matching government actions to incident severity, requires incident reporting, and preserves forensic records to learn from failures. It has received support from AI policy groups emphasizing the need for control systems to build trust and safety as AI capabilities advance. The bill reflects bipartisan concern over AI risks and seeks to provide clear authority and processes to prevent AI systems from causing serious harm or escaping human oversight.

entry.title: AI companies avoid training on AI-generated content to prevent model collapse; human-generated data remains preferred for AI training [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: AI companies are deliberately avoiding AI-generated content for training their models to prevent "model collapse," a decline in output quality caused by training AI on AI data. They prefer human-generated content, such as pre-2022 books and Reddit posts, to maintain diversity and accuracy in AI outputs. This practice highlights concerns about the homogenization of ideas and reduced creativity when AI-generated content circulates back into training data through human intermediaries. Studies show that while AI-assisted writing can boost individual creativity, it also leads to convergence of ideas and reduced diversity across writers, mirroring the effects of model collapse. The article emphasizes the importance of maintaining high-quality, human-generated training data to sustain AI reliability and warns about the risks of feedback loops involving AI-influenced human content.

entry.title: Report: MTTR is outdated for AI-driven engineering teams as it fails to capture new failure modes and code deployment speeds [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: MTTR (mean time to recovery) has been the primary metric for measuring software failure recovery for over a decade, rooted in DevOps and site reliability engineering practices. However, with AI accelerating code generation and deployment, MTTR no longer adequately reflects the speed or impact of failures in modern engineering environments. Experts argue that organizations should shift focus to metrics like mean time to failure (MTTF) to better protect customer experience and adapt to AI-era challenges. MTTR emerged alongside distributed computing and was popularized by frameworks like DORA and Google's SRE teams, emphasizing recovery speed after inevitable failures. Yet, as AI-generated code introduces new risks and faster failure cycles, relying solely on MTTR can mislead organizations due to Goodhart's Law, where metrics become targets and lose their effectiveness. The article suggests rethinking recovery metrics to align with current software production realities and safeguard user experience more effectively.

entry.title: Fable 5 leads handwritten-edit benchmark while Opus 4.8 shows 55% regression on miscounting errors [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: A new benchmark evaluates multimodal language models on their ability to interpret handwritten editorial corrections in printed text, using annotated scans from Charles Dickens' "Little Dorrit." The task challenges models to detect and interpret various editorial marks such as insertions, deletions, replacements, punctuation changes, capitalization corrections, and italicization. Fable 5 ranks first in this benchmark, demonstrating superior accuracy in capturing human editing intentions. In contrast, Opus 4.8 exhibits a 55% performance regression due to miscounting errors. The benchmark involves models analyzing scanned pages with handwritten annotations and outputting structured JSON detailing each edit's type, location, and corrected text, combining visual recognition with natural language understanding.

entry.title: Sierra Acquires Agent Startup 'Takeoff' to Diversify Its Business [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: In 2020, 22-year-old Aakash Thumaty was a product manager at Salesforce when he wrote an essay, "Value Driven Innovation at Shopify and the Incumbency Trap at Salesforce," which argued against Salesforce's subscription-based business model. He sent it to Bret Taylor, who at the time was Salesforce's chief operating officer. To Thumaty's surprise, Taylor shared it with other executives at the company. Six years later, Thumaty and Taylor's paths are crossing again. Sierra, the AI customer support startup Taylor now leads, is acquiring Thumaty's three-person startup, Takeoff, which develops agents that can work on tasks for long periods of time, the companies told The Information exclusively. They wouldn't disclose details but it's unlikely to have been a high priced acquisition. Takeoff was founded a year ago and was closing in on $10 million in annualized revenue earlier this month, Thumaty said. (It had previously raised $15 million in funding from Matrix and venture capitalist Lachy Groom.) But Sierra executives hope Thumaty's expertise will come in handy as the company tries to move beyond AI-powered customer support agents into selling agents for other tasks.

entry.title: GPT-5.5 Scores 10.6% on ActiveVision, Humans Hit 96.1% [R] [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: The interesting finding from a new [arXiv paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.16165) isn't that a frontier vision model failed a new benchmark, that happens weekly, but the specific shape of the failure and the fact that the models cannot patch it by writing their own code. The benchmark, called ActiveVision, contains 17 tasks across 3 categories designed, in the authors' words, to "force repeated visual perception rather than a single static description." GPT-5.5 at the highest exposed reasoning-effort tier solves 10.6% of items and scores zero on 11 of the 17 tasks. Claude Fable 5, which the authors note tops most reasoning and coding leaderboards, manages 3.5%. Three human participants averaged 96.1%. submitted by /u/Justgototheeffinmoon [link] [comments]
